red_flags.issue: No legal or regulated definition; can mean anything or nothing
Natural does not mean safe, sustainable, or non-toxic
Unregulated marketing term with no verification standard
Vague unless tied to a specific certification or measurable metric
Often relies on unverified or low-quality carbon offsets rather than actual emission reduction
Meaningless without specifying conditions (time, environment) required to degrade
Marketing language with no measurable or certifiable standard
No regulatory body verifies this claim
No standardized definition of 'clean' in most jurisdictions
Vague unless a specific certification or traceability system is named
Misleading if percentage of recycled content is not disclosed
Unregulated in many countries; can be claimed without third-party verification
No standardized legal definition; toxicity thresholds vary widely
Rarely independently audited; often refers only to part of the supply chain
Generic claim with no measurable backing
Common fast-fashion marketing term without third-party verification
Long-term pledges are often unverifiable and lack interim accountability
Scientifically misleading; all matter is made of chemicals
No standardized certification exists for this claim
Stronger than carbon neutral but rarely independently verified
